newsitem.title: USA: N.J. race track owner names Coelho new chairman.
newsitem.headline: N.J. race track owner names Coelho new chairman.

text.p: Former House Majority Whip Tony Coelho was named chairman of International Thoroughbred Breeders Inc., the horse racing track and hotel-casino owner announced Wednesday.

International Thoroughbred also named as chief executive Nunzio DeSantis, who with Coelho recently bought a 23 percent stake in the Cherry Hill, N.J.-based company for $11.6 million from financier Robert Brennan through their company, NPD Inc.

Brennan, who founded International Thoroughbred in 1981, was hit with a $71.5 million fine in 1995 in connection with stock fraud allegations brought by federal regulators involving his company, First Jersey Securities Inc.
Brennan, who is in bankruptcy, resigned as chairman of International Thoroughbred about a year ago and was ordered by New Jersey casino regulators to sell his stock in the company by Jan. 6.
International Thoroughbred also said it has a preliminary proposal from SunAmerica Investments, a unit of Los Angeles-based SunAmerica Inc., for a $100 million loan.
The loan is subject to court approval of the sale of the 2.9 million shares held by Brennan and a definitive agreement, it said.
Proceeds from the loan are expected to be used to reopen the shuttered El Rancho Hotel and Casino in Las Vegas and improve Garden State Park, a throughbred track in Cherry Hill, N.J..
DeSantis said that with the financing, El Rancho will be renamed Countryland USA and promoted as a major hotel-casino.

Coelho represented California in the House of Representatives from 1979 to 1989, attaining the rank of Democratic majority whip before resigning. He is a former chairman of the New York-based Wertheim Schroder Investment Services Inc. and currently heads his own investment consulting firm.
DeSantis founded Diagnostek Inc., an Albuquerque, N.M.-based pharmacy management company which was sold in 1995 for $500 million.
